open_points.subject: orphan value-byte reuse and startup cleanup
open_points.text: “value bytes are reused by equal bytes until the next start removes them” conflicts with “On start, … value bytes no record names … are removed; nothing else is.”
open_points.question: If a later successful store call reuses value bytes left by a failed call and records a reference to them before restart, does the next start preserve them because they are now named, or remove them because rule 3 says the next start removes them?
options: Preserve bytes that are named at startup
Remove every value file originally published by a failed call
Do not allow an orphan value file to be adopted by a later successful call
open_points.default_guess: Preserve the bytes when any record names them at startup.

open_points.subject: startup removal of unreferenced value bytes
open_points.text: “On start, … value bytes no record names … are removed” gives no result when one of those files cannot be removed; only an unremovable ended-run spool directory is explicitly allowed to remain without stopping startup.
open_points.question: What happens when startup cannot remove an unreferenced value-byte file: does startup fail, continue while leaving it unserved for a later start, or continue with another specified treatment?
options: Continue and leave the file unserved until a later start
Continue but quarantine or otherwise mark the file
open_points.default_guess: Continue, never serve the unreferenced file, and retry removal at a later start.
